newsitem.title: IRAQ: Italian diplomats in Iraq to open interest section.
newsitem.headline: Italian diplomats in Iraq to open interest section.

text.p: Four Italian diplomats have arrived in Iraq to open an interest section for the first time since the 1991 Gulf War, a diplomatic source in Baghdad said on Saturday.
The source said the section would open under the Hungarian flag but gave no date.
"(Head of section) Cesare Ragaglini and the other three Italian diplomats arrived in Baghdad on Friday to open an interest section," the source told Reuters.
Last week an Italian official, who was invited by the Iraqi government, said Baghdad had sent a diplomat to Rome to head an Iraqi interest section there working under the Sudanese flag.
"Qais al-Yakoubi who will head the Iraqi interest section in Rome has left Baghdad," said Antonio Loche, Secretary-General of the government-funded Italian Institute for Asia.
Italy, Baghdad's fourth largest trading partner before the war, sent a mission in February to Iraq to look at opening an interest section in Baghdad in the Hungarian embassy.
Iraq severed diplomatic ties with Italy and Arab and Western countries which took part in the U.S.-led military coalition which drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1990.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini announced in July that the planned interest section would be opened.

Iraq is under stringent U.N. trade sanction imposed on it after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The curbs include a ban on Iraq's oil exports and imports of all commodities except for food and medicine, for which Iraq has little cash.
The U.N. Security Council retained on Friday the sanctions, mainly because it says Baghdad has not fully detailed its manufacturing programmes for weapons of mass destruction.
